reading.title: The Future of Space Exploration
reading.text: Space agencies and private companies are planning ambitious missions to return humans to the Moon and eventually reach Mars. NASA's Artemis program aims to land the first woman and next man on the lunar surface by 2026. Meanwhile, SpaceX is developing the Starship rocket, designed to carry up to 100 passengers on interplanetary journeys. One of the biggest challenges is radiation exposure during long flights, which can increase cancer risk for astronauts. Scientists are working on new shielding materials and even pharmaceutical countermeasures. Another challenge is the psychological strain of living in confined spaces for years. Despite these obstacles, the dream of becoming a multi-planetary species continues to drive innovation.

reading.title: The Lost City of Petra
reading.text: Carved directly into rose-red cliffs in the Jordanian desert, Petra flourished as the capital of the Nabataean kingdom from the 4th century BCE. The city was strategically located on trade routes linking Arabia, Egypt, and Syria, making it wealthy and powerful. Petra's most famous structure, Al-Khazneh (The Treasury), features an elaborate facade inspired by Greek architecture. The city declined after the Romans annexed the Nabataean kingdom and trade routes shifted to sea routes. Eventually, Petra was abandoned and remained unknown to the Western world until Swiss explorer Johann Ludwig Burckhardt rediscovered it in 1812.

options: Roman annexation and shift to sea routes

reading.title: The Science of Sleep
reading.text: Sleep is essential for memory consolidation, immune function, and emotional regulation. During sleep, the brain cycles through different stages, including REM (Rapid Eye Movement) and non-REM sleep. REM sleep is when most dreaming occurs and is crucial for processing emotions and learning. Non-REM sleep, particularly deep sleep, allows the body to repair tissues and strengthen the immune system. Chronic sleep deprivation has been linked to obesity, heart disease, and impaired cognitive function. Experts recommend that adults get 7-9 hours of quality sleep per night, yet many people fail to meet this goal due to screen time and stress.

options: Memory consolidation, immune function, emotional regulation
